_comment: Help for each command, shown by `clickruntime <command> --help` and `clickruntime help <command>`. scripts/generate.mjs embeds it in both CLIs; edit here, then run node scripts/generate.mjs.

status.summary: Shows whether this machine is signed in to ClickRuntime, and as whom. Run it first.
status.output: {signed_in, email, profile_id, workspace_profile, api_url, token_source} or {signed_in: false, next}
status.exits: 0 signed in, 3 not signed in (next.action is login)

login.summary: Signs in. The person approves in the browser; you never handle a password or key.
details: Without flags it opens the browser. If no sign-in arrives within 5 minutes it also prints a link and a code, and keeps waiting for either.
Give the person the link and the code exactly as printed. They type the code on the page.
flags: Use a link and a code instead of opening a browser (remote machines, sandboxes).
Print the link and code and exit 4 instead of waiting. Then run login --continue.
Keep waiting for a sign-in started with --no-wait.
login.output: {signed_in: true, email} or, while waiting, {state: "waiting", user_code, next: {url, say}}
login.exits: 0 signed in, 4 waiting (with --no-wait), 6 denied, cancelled or expired

logout.summary: Signs out on this machine and ends this sign-in in the ClickRuntime dashboard.

init.summary: Writes clickruntime.json and a starter automation.py for a new automation. Nothing is sent yet.
details: schedule: runs on a schedule. incoming: runs when an event arrives on its trigger link. remember_then_schedule: runs on a schedule and keeps state between runs.
Fill in summary and how_it_works in clickruntime.json, write automation.py (see clickruntime docs runtime), then save.
flags: Folder to write to (default: the current folder).
init.exits: 0, 2 if the folder already has an automation

save.summary: Sends clickruntime.json and automation.py. The first save creates a draft and writes its automation_id into clickruntime.json; later saves update it.
details: Saving a live automation stores a pending change; it goes live only after deploy and the person's confirmation.
Read notes in the output: they point out problems the server found in the script.
flags: Folder with clickruntime.json and automation.py (default: the current folder).
save.output: The automation: {automation_id, name, status, notes, next}
save.exits: 0, 2 if the files are missing or invalid

pull.summary: Writes an existing automation's clickruntime.json and automation.py so you can change it and save again.
details: Saved key values are never included. Check setup_needs before saving.
flags: Folder to write to (default: the current folder).

show.summary: Shows one automation: status, schedule or trigger link, pending change and what to do next.

setup.usage:
clickruntime setup <automation_id>
clickruntime setup run --title <title> [--purpose discover|setup] [--file automation.py] [--changes <text>]
setup.summary: setup <id> lists what the person still has to add (keys, connections), each with a link to the ClickRuntime dashboard. setup run runs a one-off script with the workspace's connections, to look things up or prepare a service.
details: Give the person each link. Never ask them to paste a key into the chat or a command.
setup run reads setup_needs and dependencies from clickruntime.json in the current folder.
flags: setup run: a short title the person sees.
setup run: discover (read only, the default) or setup (may change things in a service).
setup run: the script to run (default: automation.py).
setup run with --purpose setup: what the script will change, in plain words.
setup.output: setup: {ready, items: [{name, ready, url}], next}. setup run: {setup_run_id, status, logs, error}
setup.exits: setup: 0 ready, 4 waiting on the person. setup run: 0 succeeded, 1 failed or timed out

deploy.summary: Asks the person to confirm turning on a draft, applying a pending change, or resuming a paused automation, then waits for the deploy.
details: Prints a confirm link. Give it to the person; only they can confirm. Never open it yourself.
By default it waits (up to --timeout, 600 s). With --json it returns at once unless you pass --wait; then run clickruntime wait <confirmation_ref>.
flags: Wait for the confirmation even with --json.
Return the confirm link at once (exit 4).
deploy.output: Waiting: {confirmation_ref, links: {confirm}, next}. Done: {state: "confirmed", confirmation, automation}
deploy.exits: 0 confirmed and deployed, 4 still waiting on the person, 6 cancelled or expired
deploy.next: clickruntime run <id> to try it, then clickruntime runs <id>

run.summary: Asks the person to confirm one run now, then waits for the confirmation.
details: Same confirm link flow as deploy.
flags: Wait for the confirmation even with --json.
Return the confirm link at once (exit 4).

resume.summary: Asks the person to confirm resuming a paused automation.

delete.summary: Asks the person to confirm deleting an automation. It cannot be undone.

wait.summary: Keeps waiting for the person to confirm, after deploy, run, resume or delete returned exit 4.
wait.output: {state: "confirmed", confirmation, automation} or the confirmation status while waiting
wait.exits: 0 confirmed, 4 still waiting, 6 cancelled or expired

pause.summary: Pauses a live automation. Needs no confirmation.
pause.next: clickruntime resume <id> to turn it back on

flags: Only runs in this state, such as failed.

run-log.summary: Shows one run: status, logs and error.
flags: Wait for a run that is still going to finish.

events.summary: Lists events received on an incoming automation's trigger link.

replay.summary: Runs a live or paused automation again on an event it already received.

test-event.summary: Sends a test event to an incoming automation. A draft runs it right away; a live one asks the person to confirm first.
flags: JSON file with the event body.
test-event.output: The test run, or a confirm link with next

connections.summary: Lists the names of saved keys and the connected apps in this workspace. Never the values.

connect.summary: Gets a link where the person connects an app (such as gmail or slack) in the ClickRuntime dashboard.
details: Give the person the link. clickruntime apps lists the apps.
flags: Name for this connection, when there is more than one account.
The automation this connection is for.
connect.exits: 0 already connected, 4 waiting on the person

apps.summary: Lists the apps an automation can connect to.

docs.summary: Prints a guide as markdown. cli: this CLI (sign-in, the build and go-live flow, output, exit codes, settings). runtime: how to write automation.py (the SDK, triggers, state, limits).

issue.usage:
clickruntime issue report --title <t> --body <text> [--category bug|connection|billing|other] [--automation <id>] [--run <run_id>]
clickruntime issue list
clickruntime issue show <issue_id>
clickruntime issue reply <issue_id> --body <text>
issue.summary: Reports a problem to ClickRuntime support and follows up on it.
flags: report and reply: what happened, in plain words. Never include keys.
report: bug, connection, billing or other (default).
report: the automation it is about.
report: the run it is about.

help.summary: Shows the command list, or help for one command (the same as clickruntime <command> --help).
